items.title: John LaPorta interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Was there a noticeable difference at the time between let’s say the bands like Glenn Miller and the white oriented bands and Basie and Ellington that you can talk about?

ctx.x: The times change. People don’t. The characteristics that people have, you know the competitiveness and the things that go into play for things to happen. But music answers different needs at different times you know. I know a lot of the older musicians feel like well, this is, the music now is not any good, of course most of those people, and I’m probably a product of that too, go down memory lane, and they associate the music that was part of their roots and part of their beginnings, so the young people have…
Was there a noticeable difference at the time between let’s say the bands like Glenn Miller and the white oriented bands and Basie and Ellington that you can talk about?

Well there certainly was. A good example would be Dixieland music. I never realized until I made a study, I wanted to do a New Orleans concert at the school after being there for twenty-five years and never having seen one at Berklee, I guess it was a modern school for that time, I decided to do a New Orleans concert. And the students really loved it because it was so different from what they heard there. But in the process of preparing for it, I got to realize that the thing about feeling music in four-four…
